ai.mechanism: Evidence shows only that the entire USDC balance (789,437.589055 USDC, ~$789,438) left contract 0xd3ec0e34aa628c66083759fe35e45ccf73a76d28 on Base in one transaction. No caller, no function selector, no permission or ownership data, no protocol identity, and no pre/post state beyond the balance share. The mechanism cannot be named from this packet.
ai.lossBearer: Unidentified. The immediate balance holder is contract 0xd3ec0e34aa628c66083759fe35e45ccf73a76d28; no beneficial owner, depositor set or integrator exposure is shown in the packet.
ai.narrative: A contract on Base had its full USDC balance moved out in a single transaction: 789,437.589055 USDC, about $789,438, with 100% of the balance removed. That is all the packet establishes. There is no protocol name, no caller, no call data and no sign of whether the mover was authorised. A treasury sweep, a bridge settlement or a contract migration produces exactly this shape on chain, and so does a theft. The integrator list is empty, so no downstream party is shown to be carrying the loss. Until someone can show the transfer was unauthorised, this should be treated as an unexplained movement, not a confirmed exploit.
